text:
Mike R: Heads-up customers reporting p99 latency spike for /v1/generate in eu-west since ~14:10 UTC. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123... p50 stable, p95 up 2x, p99 jumped to ~3.4s. Affects streaming and non-streaming. :warning:
SRE Oncall: alerted by ops-bot. Confirmed spike on host pools eu-west-1a/b. Any recent rollouts? :eyes:
Tara K: I rolled model shard swap at 14:05 for model redwood-medium-v2 to fix memory fragmentation. Could be related. Rolling back now.
Sam (runtime): logs show a backlog in tokenize workers and long blocking in kv-cache fetches. Patch queued to disable eager KV fetch for this model.
Julia (support): Customer ACME reported timeouts and partial responses, opened support ticket #4321. They provided repro: 800 concurrent streaming sessions with 24k context.
SRE Oncall: Repro steps noted. Immediate mitigations we can try now:
- Apply route-level rate limit for /v1/generate for hosted tier to 1200 rps
- Enable circuit breaker: set max_pending=60, max_latency_ms=2000 for eu-west
- Route heavy customers to fallback model small-redwood-1.0 (lower mem, lower latency)
- Rollback model swap if it correlates
Commands:
```bash
# rate limit via control plane
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","region":"eu-west","rate_per_min":72000}'

# set circuit breaker via redwoodctl
redwoodctl policies set --region eu-west --route /v1/generate \
  --circuit-breaker "max_pending=60,max_latency_ms=2000,fallback_model=small-redwood-1.0"

# quick routing change to fallback model
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-west --route /v1/generate --model small-redwood-1.0 --weight 1.0 --note "p99 mitigation"
```
Sam (runtime): I'm pushing a hotfix to avoid eager KV lookups; will also increase worker pool for tokenizer by +3 instances in eu-west.
Tara K: Rollback done at 14:20. Initial look: p99 decreased to ~2.1s but still above SLO. Continuing with circuit breaker and rate limits.
SRE Oncall: Ops-bot pushed rate-limits and routing. Monitoring.
ops-bot: ALERT cleared? partial. p95 trending down to 900ms, p99 at 1.8s. :thumbsup:
Patrick P: Need customer communication. Julia, can you send affected customers a note: short blurb, mitigation steps, ETA?
Julia (support): On it. Drafting: "We've observed increased latencies in eu-west affecting long-context streaming. We're applying temporary rate limits and routing to lower-latency model; no data loss. ETA 30-60m for full recovery." Will post in status page and notify ACME.
SRE Oncall: Post-incident follow-ups / playbook updates:
- Add explicit playbook entry: 'eu-west p99 spike' with checklist (rate-limit, circuit-break, fallback-route, rollback, tokenizer scale)
- Add automated runbook action in control plane: one-click enforce circuit-breaker + fallback route
- Add SLO guardrail: auto-throttle for tenants > X rps when p95 > 800ms for 5m
- Add observability alert: new alert for p95>800ms AND p99>1500ms in region
Sam (runtime): PR for hotfix and worker scale is ready, deploying to eu-west-prod-canary.
Tara K: Repro notes for postmortem: heavy-context streaming + concurrent warm-up + model swap triggered higher KV cache misses and tokenizer bottleneck. Steps to reproduce locally:
1) spawn 800 concurrent clients
2) send 24k token context with streaming enabled
3) keep connections open and interleave 50ms token delays
Expected: p99 ~ <1s, Observed: p99 2-3.5s
SRE Oncall: Keep monitor until 15:00 UTC. If p99 doesn't reach <1s, escalate to infra to add temporary capacity. Good work team. :pray:
Patrick P: Add a postmortem and add capacity playbook to Dedicated customers note.
Julia (support): Status update posted. Notifying ACME and other affected customers.
SRE Oncall: last check 14:45 UTC: p95 650ms, p99 980ms. Closing thread for now but will open a postmortem ticket and link runbook.
Mike R: Thanks all. We'll follow up with action items in the postmortem. :rocket:
